question.prompt: Pablo, Sofia, and Mia got some candy eggs at a party. Pablo had three times as many eggs as Sofia, and Sofia had twice as many eggs as Mia. Pablo decides to give some of his eggs to Sofia and Mia so that all three will have the same number of eggs. What fraction of his eggs should Pablo give to Sofia?

solutions.explanation:
Use Mia's original number of eggs as one unit. Sofia then has \(2\) units, and Pablo has \(3\cdot2=6\) units. Their original amounts are therefore in the ratio \(6:2:1\).

Giving eggs to one another preserves the total of \(6+2+1=9\) units. To finish equally, each person must have \(9/3=3\) units. Sofia needs \(3-2=1\) unit, while Mia needs \(3-1=2\) units. Pablo can give these amounts and retain \(6-1-2=3\) units.

Sofia receives one of Pablo's original six equal units, so the requested fraction is \(\boxed{\frac16}\), choice B.
solutions.title: Use proportional units
